items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: Because Herbie Hancock, he’s written some beautiful songs, and Wayne Shorter.

ctx.x: No. Like I said I did “Expansions” and it just took off, and then “A Garden of Peace.” Because that’s what happens, as you know the record companies put a lot of pressure on you, you know ‘cause everybody wants a gold record or a platinum record. And so that was one reason I was in the studio that day and I wrote “A Garden of Peace” I said, oh shoot, I just want to do something beautiful and peaceful. And like years later it paid off. So but I — oh Bob Thiele used to always mess with me. He said man look why…

cosmic, come on now.” And he’d do it on purpose, you know but like I say I was just fortunate and blessed you know that these songs just took off and stood on their own. Because Herbie Hancock, he’s written some beautiful songs, and Wayne Shorter. So I don’t think they was trying to write hits but they became hits.
Yeah. That’s the best way for it to happen I think.
